title: Silent Letters (d, e, g, h, p, s, t, x)

sections.html: Many French letters are written but not pronounced, especially at the end of words.

sections.heading: General rule: final consonants are usually silent
The "CaReFuL" exception
sections.html:
Final C, R, F, L are usually pronounced: - c: avec, sac, parc - r: bonjour, hiver, car - f: neuf, chef, actif - l: avril, sel, journal

Exceptions: the -er of infinitives is pronounced "ay" with a silent r (parler, manger); blanc, estomac (silent c); gentil (silent l).

sections.heading: Silent **e**
sections.html:
• A final e without an accent is silent: table, rouge, France.
  • But it makes the consonant before it pronounced: petit (silent t) vs petite (t pronounced). This is how you hear the feminine of many adjectives.

sections.heading: Silent **h**
sections.html: The h is never pronounced in French. There are two kinds: - h muet (mute h): the word behaves as if it starts with a vowel. You use l' and make liaisons: l'homme, l'hôtel, les‿hommes (lez-om). - h aspiré (aspirated h): still silent, but it blocks elision and liaison: le héros, la haine, les | haricots (lay ah-ree-ko, no z). Dictionaries mark these with an asterisk or apostrophe.

sections.heading: Silent endings of verbs
sections.html:
• -ent in the 3rd person plural of verbs is silent: ils parlent sounds exactly like il parle.
  • -es, -e also silent: tu parles, je parle all sound the same.

sections.heading: Liaison: when a silent consonant wakes up
sections.html:
When a word ending in a silent consonant is followed by a word starting with a vowel or mute h, the consonant is often pronounced and linked: - les‿amis (lay-z-ah-mee) — s sounds like z - vous‿avez (voo-z-ah-vay) - petit‿enfant (puh-tee-t-ahn-fahn) - deux‿heures (duh-z-uhr) — x sounds like z

Liaison is required after articles (les, des, un), pronouns (nous, vous, ils), and short adjectives before nouns. It is forbidden after et (et | elle).

exercises.prompt: Do these two sound the same or different? *il mange* / *ils mangent*.
Is there a liaison? (a) *les enfants* (b) *et alors* (c) *vous habitez*.
Why is the *t* pronounced in *petite* but not *petit*?
exercises.answer: The final silent **e** makes the preceding consonant pronounced.
